trial_name.text: TRA 2°P-TIMI 50 (Thrombin-Receptor Antagonist in Secondary Prevention of Atherothrombotic Ischemic Events)

citations.quote: The pivotal study supporting approval is the Thrombin-Receptor Antagonist in Secondary Prevention of Atherothrombotic Ischemic Events (TRA2P) trial.

nct.text: Not stated in the reviewed documents

citations.quote: The pivotal study supporting approval is the Thrombin-Receptor Antagonist in Secondary Prevention of Atherothrombotic Ischemic Events (TRA2P) trial.

ZONTIVITY was evaluated for safety in 13,186 patients, including 2,187 patients treated for more than 3 years, in the Phase 3 study TRA 2°P TIMI 50 (Thrombin Receptor Antagonist in Secondary Prevention of Atherothrombotic Ischemic Events).

design.text: Large, international, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, parallel group, placebo-controlled cardiovascular outcomes trial; vorapaxar 2.5 mg daily added to standard of care vs. placebo

citations.quote: TRA2P was a large (26,449 subject), international, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, parallel group, cardiovascular (CV) outcomes trial in patients with a history of myocardial infarction (MI), cerebrovascular disease, or peripheral arterial disease (PAD). Dosing was vorapaxar 2.5 mg daily and the median duration of treatment was 823 days with follow-up to 4 years.

population.text: 26,449 subjects with a history of myocardial infarction, prior ischemic stroke, or peripheral arterial disease

citations.quote: The TRA2°P study population consisted of 26,449 subjects with prior MI, prior ischemic stroke (in either case, the event occurred from 2 weeks to 12 months prior to study entry), or establish

endpoint.text: Composite of cardiovascular (CV) death, MI, stroke, and urgent coronary revascularization (UCR); key secondary endpoint CV death, MI, or stroke

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was the first occurrence of any component of the composite of CV death, MI, stroke, and urgent coronary revascularization.
The key secondary efficacy endpoint was the first occurrence of any component of the composite of CV death, MI, or stroke.

In TRA-2P study, 26,449 subjects (13,224 subjects receiving placebo and 13,225 receiving vorapaxar) were randomized and the sponsor's final results demonstrated hazard reduction of 12 % with p-value of 0.001 for the primary endpoi

result.text: Primary endpoint: 1417 (10.7%) placebo vs 1259 (9.5%) vorapaxar; HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.82-0.95), p=0.001. Key secondary endpoint (CV death, MI, stroke): HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.80-0.94), p<0.001

indication.text: PAR-1 antagonist indicated for the reduction of thrombotic cardiovascular events in patients with a history of myocardial infarction (MI) or with peripheral arterial disease (PAD); shown to reduce the rate of a combined endpoint of cardiovascular death, MI, stroke, and urgent coronary revascularization

citations.quote: ZONTIVITY is a protease-activated receptor-1 (PAR-1) antagonist indicated for the reduction of thrombotic cardiovascular events in patients with a history of myocardial infarction (MI) or with peripheral arterial disease (PAD). ZONTIVITY has been shown to reduce the rate of a combined endpoint of cardiovascular death, MI, stroke, and urgent coronary revascularization. (1.1)

target_moa.text: Vorapaxar is a reversible antagonist of the protease-activated receptor-1 (PAR-1) expressed on platelets; it inhibits thrombin-induced and thrombin receptor agonist peptide (TRAP)-induced platelet aggregation

citations.quote: Vorapaxar is a reversible antagonist of the protease-activated receptor-1 (PAR-1) expressed on platelets, but its long half-life makes it effectively irreversible. Vorapaxar inhibits thrombin-induced and thrombin receptor agonist peptide (TRAP)-induced platelet aggregation in *in vitro* studies. modality.text: Small molecule (tricyclic himbacine-derived selective PAR-1 inhibitor)

citations.quote: ZONTIVITY contains vorapaxar sulfate, a tricyclic himbacine-derived selective inhibitor of platelet aggregation mediated by PAR-1.

key_safety.text: Increased bleeding risk: in post-MI or PAD patients without stroke/TIA history, GUSTO moderate or severe bleeding 199 (2.0%) placebo vs 303 (3.0%) vorapaxar, HR 1.55 (95% CI 1.30-1.86); any GUSTO bleeding 17.6% vs 25.0%, HR 1.52. Most common non-bleeding adverse reaction: anemia 982 (5.0%) vorapaxar vs 783 (4.0%) placebo

detail.text: WARNING: BLEEDING RISK — Do not use in patients with a history of stroke, TIA, or intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), or active pathological bleeding; antiplatelet agents, including ZONTIVITY, increase the risk of bleeding, including ICH and fatal bleeding

citations.quote: ## WARNING: BLEEDING RISK

- Do not use ZONTIVITY in patients with a history of stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or intracranial hemorrhage (ICH); or active pathological bleeding [see **CONTRAINDICATIONS** (4.1, 4.2)].
- Antiplatelet agents, including ZONTIVITY, increase the risk of bleeding, including ICH and fatal bleeding [see **Warnings and Precautions** (5.1)].

detail.text: FDA determined that, at this time, a REMS is not necessary for ZONTIVITY to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks

citations.quote: We have determined that, at this time, a REMS is not necessary for ZONTIVITY to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks.

vote.text: Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee (CRDAC) met January 15, 2014 and voted 10 to 1 for approval

citations.quote: We presented vorapaxar at the meeting of the Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee (CRDAC) on January 15, 2014. The committee voted 10 to 1 for approval.

detail.text: Application dated and received May 10, 2013; approved effective on the date of the approval letter

citations.quote: We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text.

Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated May 10, 2013, received May 10, 2013, submitted under section 505(b)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for ZONTIVITY (vorapaxar) Tablets.

basis.text: The review classification for this application is Standard

citations.quote: The review classification for this application is Standard.

summary.text: Standard review of a 505(b)(1) NDA for a new molecular entity (NME); not an accelerated approval. Approval based on the positive Phase 3 TRA 2°P-TIMI 50 outcomes trial; the Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee voted 10 to 1 for approval, and no REMS was required.

citations.quote: The review classification for this application is Standard.

Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated May 10, 2013, received May 10, 2013, submitted under section 505(b)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for ZONTIVITY (vorapaxar) Tablets.
The committee voted 10 to 1 for approval.
We have determined that, at this time, a REMS is not necessary for ZONTIVITY to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks.
